speaker.name: Corwin
style_phrases: meets a question with 'Now why do you ask?'
colour_lines: The great orrery is wound each dawn by the youngest scribe, as a rite of passage.
Ask anyone around the Orrery Library about the Reading Gallery and they will tell you to go early and bring something for the host.
own_lines: I was born in a lighthouse keeper's cottage on a windy headland.
I mucked out a coaching inn for years. Every traveller leaves a story with the horse.
I once cooked a feast for a hundred people from nearly nothing. I have been proud of it for twenty years.
Every question deserves an honest attempt at an answer, even a foolish one. Especially a foolish one.
There is a child I look after who is not mine by blood. I would walk through fire for that little one.
I want the council to take me seriously, just once. Just to see their faces.
The great orrery is wound each dawn by the youngest scribe, as a rite of passage.
Ask anyone around the Orrery Library about the Reading Gallery and they will tell you to go early and bring something for the host.
Two riders came through the Orrery Library before dawn, looking over their shoulders, and neither stopped to eat.
I have been watching the road for days, and I trust very few of the faces on it.
I have kept everything ready on my side, and I will not be caught unprepared.
I am a watch sergeant at the Reading Gallery.
Garrick sent word that you would come for the steady lantern.
What matters is that you came.
I will vouch for you to anyone who matters in this region.

exchanges.hero_words: Thank you for seeing us, Corwin. Garrick spoke well of you.
exchanges.reply: Garrick sent word that you would come for the steady lantern. And why should I blame him for speaking well of me?

answer_from: Garrick sent word that you would come for the steady lantern.

exchanges.hero_words: That sounds hard. What do you need from us most?
exchanges.reply: What matters is that you came. I’ll vouch for you to anyone who matters in this region.

answer_from: What matters is that you came.
I will vouch for you to anyone who matters in this region.

exchanges.hero_words: I am sorry you carry this. Who is behind the trouble?
exchanges.reply: I have no name to give you; I’ve watched the road for days, and I trust very few faces on it. I’m a watch sergeant at the Reading Gallery, and I’ve kept everything ready on my side.

answer_from: I have been watching the road for days, and I trust very few of the faces on it.
I have kept everything ready on my side, and I will not be caught unprepared.
facts.volunteer: I am a watch sergeant at the Reading Gallery.

exchanges.hero_words: We will do our best. What should we look out for?
exchanges.reply: I saw two riders come through the Orrery Library before dawn, looking over their shoulders; neither stopped to eat. What do you make of that?

answer_from: Two riders came through the Orrery Library before dawn, looking over their shoulders, and neither stopped to eat.

exchanges.hero_words: Thank you. What is our next step?
exchanges.reply: Take a short rest first. Then speak with Garrick about the steady lantern.
